answer: Copying the same citations across 89 aliases thus pays the reading cost 89 times, while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. Because a fabricated citation fails the relic check immediately, the quartz audit keeps the resolved set and the atlas replay reveals exactly which ids were live. An answer must cite at least 5 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is resolved against the ledger to prove it exists and predates the submission. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
